section_summary.extract_value: This section reports correlation results: early memories of warmth and safeness (EMWSS) are positively associated with self-compassion (weak) and body appreciation (moderate), and negatively associated with eating-disorder symptoms (EDE-Q, weak). Self-compassion and body appreciation are positively interrelated and both negatively correlate with EDE-Q. Age showed non-significant associations with body appreciation and EDE-Q, positive correlations with BMI (moderate) and self-compassion (weak), and a negative weak relationship with EMWSS; BMI was negatively associated with EMWSS and body appreciation and positively with EDE-Q (moderate). No study numbering or sample/sample-source details are provided in the text; descriptive statistics are referenced as being in Table 1.
section_summary.evidence_source: The descriptive statistics for the study variables are presented on Table 1. Correlations analysis' results showed that early memories of warmth and safeness were positively associated to self-compassion and body appreciation, with weak and moderate magnitudes, respectively. Finally, BMI presented negative associations with early memories of warmth and safeness and body appreciation, and a positive link to EDE-Q, with a moderate magnitude.
